title: Avi Loeb heads up plan for new observatory to directly image UFOs
excerpt: The Harvard astrophysicist has detailed plans for a novel new way to acquire more information about UAPs.
content:
The UFO Phenomenon

By T.K. Randall
November 17, 2026


Image: AI-generated (Midjourney)

The Harvard astrophysicist has detailed plans for a novel new way to acquire more information about UAPs.

Loeb, who now heads up the US government's UAP Science Advisory Council, has reported that his idea for a way to gather high-resolution imaging and spectroscopic measurements of anomalous aerial vehicles has moved to the construction phase.

The new observatory, which will be built in Ithaca, New York and funded by entrepreneur and philanthropist Adam Weitsman, will use a combination of advanced radar technology, artificial intelligence and an astronomical telescope to find out more about these mysterious objects.

Its development marks a shift away from relying on reports of sightings that have happened in the past and on to directly observing UFOs in real-time.

The observatory will work by using radar to monitor the sky, then when an unknown object is detected, AI-assisted software will analyze it to rule out any known conventional explanations.

If none are found, the large telescope will then be directed at the object to take high-resolution photographs and spectroscopic measurements.

"Over the past six months, the US government has declassified data on numerous puzzling objects in our skies, whose nature is unknown," Loeb said in the press release.

"Rather than speculate on whether they represent natural atmospheric phenomena, birds, drones, balloons, aircraft or alien technologies of non-human origin, we should study them with state-of-the-art instruments."

"This observatory will demonstrate a new approach to collecting high-resolution images and spectroscopic data, potentially resolving this mystery with important implications for national security and fundamental science."

Source: Avi Loeb
